OPTION TO PURCHASE REAL PROPERTY

This Option to Purchase Real Property (this "Option Agreement") is made as of July 20, 2026, between Wendell Osgood Ferraro and Ilaria Ferraro, husband and wife (together, "Optionor"), and Braddock Ridge Development LLC, a Virginia limited liability company ("Optionee").

RECITALS

Optionor owns the real property located at 4180 Quarry Bend Road, Fauquier County, Virginia, consisting of approximately 61.4 acres and identified as Tax Map Parcel 6042-88-1130, together with all improvements, easements, and appurtenances (the "Property"). Optionee wishes to acquire an exclusive option to purchase the Property, and Optionor is willing to grant it on the terms below.

1. GRANT OF OPTION; CONSIDERATION

1.1 Grant. Optionor grants to Optionee the exclusive and irrevocable option to purchase the Property on the terms in this Option Agreement (the "Option").

1.2 Option Consideration. In consideration of the grant of the Option, Optionee shall pay Optionor $85,000 (the "Option Consideration") within three (3) business days after the date of this Option Agreement, the receipt and sufficiency of which Optionor acknowledges. The Option Consideration is fully earned on payment and is non-refundable under all circumstances except a default by Optionor under Section 6.2. The Option Consideration is independent consideration for the Option and is not an earnest money deposit. If Optionee exercises the Option, the Option Consideration is credited against the Purchase Price at closing.

2. OPTION PERIOD AND EXERCISE

2.1 Option Period. The Option may be exercised at any time from the date of this Option Agreement through 5:00 p.m. Eastern time on July 20, 2029 (the "Option Period"). Time is of the essence with respect to every date and deadline in this Option Agreement.

2.2 Extension. Optionee may extend the Option Period by one additional twelve-month term by delivering written notice of extension, together with an extension payment of $40,000, on or before the last day of the initial Option Period. The extension payment is non-refundable and is credited against the Purchase Price at closing.

2.3 Exercise. Optionee exercises the Option by delivering written notice of exercise to Optionor on or before the last day of the Option Period. Notice must be delivered by hand, by nationally recognized overnight courier, or by certified mail, return receipt requested, to Optionor at 4180 Quarry Bend Road, Warrenton, Virginia 20186, with a courtesy copy by email to wferraro@quarrybendfarm.com. Notice by email alone is not effective. Notice is effective on delivery, or, if delivered after 5:00 p.m. Eastern time, on the next business day. An exercise notice that is late, conditional, or qualified is ineffective, and the Option expires.

2.4 Expiration. If Optionee does not exercise the Option within the Option Period, the Option terminates automatically, Optionor retains the Option Consideration and any extension payment, and neither party has any further obligation except under Section 4.3 and Section 7.

3. PURCHASE PRICE AND CLOSING

3.1 Purchase Price. The purchase price for the Property is $2,940,000, subject to adjustment under Section 3.2 (the "Purchase Price").

3.2 Adjustment. If the Option is exercised during the extension term, the Purchase Price increases to the greater of (a) $2,940,000 and (b) the fair market value of the Property as of the exercise date, determined by an MAI appraiser jointly selected by the parties within fifteen (15) days after exercise. If the parties do not agree on an appraiser, each shall appoint one MAI appraiser within ten (10) days, and the two appraisers shall appoint a third; the fair market value is the average of the two closest of the three appraisals. Each party bears the cost of its own appraiser and one half of the third appraiser's cost.

3.3 Closing. Closing occurs sixty (60) days after the exercise notice is effective, at the offices of the title company selected by Optionee in Fauquier County, Virginia. Optionor shall convey the Property by general warranty deed, free and clear of all liens and encumbrances other than the Permitted Exceptions listed on Exhibit B. Real estate taxes, rents, and assessments are prorated as of the closing date. Optionor pays the grantor's tax; Optionee pays the recording fees and all title insurance premiums.

4. COVENANTS DURING THE OPTION PERIOD

4.1 No Encumbrance or Transfer. During the Option Period, Optionor shall not sell, convey, lease, mortgage, or otherwise encumber the Property, grant any easement or option over it, or take any action that would impair the marketability of title, without Optionee's prior written consent.

4.2 Maintenance and Access. Optionor shall maintain the Property in its present condition, ordinary wear excepted, and shall keep in force the existing casualty insurance. Optionee and its agents may enter the Property on two (2) business days' notice to conduct surveys, soil tests, environmental assessments, and other due diligence.

4.3 Restoration and Indemnity. Optionee shall restore any damage caused by its entry and shall indemnify and hold Optionor harmless from any claim, lien, or damage arising from Optionee's entry on the Property. This Section 4.3 survives the expiration or termination of this Option Agreement.

5. MEMORANDUM OF OPTION

5.1 Recordation. Concurrently with this Option Agreement, the parties shall execute a memorandum of option in the short form attached as Exhibit A, which Optionee may record in the land records of the Circuit Court of Fauquier County, Virginia. The memorandum gives constructive notice of the Option to third parties and does not modify this Option Agreement.

5.2 Release. Within ten (10) business days after the expiration or termination of the Option without exercise, Optionee shall execute and deliver to Optionor a recordable release of the memorandum of option. If Optionee fails to do so, Optionor may record a copy of this Option Agreement together with an affidavit of expiration.

6. DEFAULT

6.1 Optionee Default. If Optionee exercises the Option and then fails to close, Optionor's sole remedy is to retain the Option Consideration and any extension payment as liquidated damages, the parties agreeing that actual damages would be difficult to determine.

6.2 Optionor Default. If Optionor breaches this Option Agreement, Optionee may seek specific performance, which the parties agree is an appropriate remedy because the Property is unique, or may terminate this Option Agreement and recover the Option Consideration, any extension payment, and its out-of-pocket costs.

7. GENERAL

7.1 Rule Against Perpetuities. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, the Option and every right granted by this Option Agreement terminate, if not sooner terminated, twenty-one (21) years less one day after the date of this Option Agreement, and in no event may any interest created by this Option Agreement vest later than the period permitted by the rule against perpetuities.

7.2 Assignment. Optionee may assign this Option Agreement to an entity controlled by Optionee or to a qualified intermediary for a like-kind exchange, on written notice to Optionor. Any other assignment requires Optionor's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld.

7.3 Governing Law; Forum. This Option Agreement is governed by the laws of the Commonwealth of Virginia. Any action arising out of this Option Agreement shall be brought in the Circuit Court of Fauquier County, Virginia.

7.4 Entire Agreement; Amendment; Counterparts. This Option Agreement, with Exhibit A and Exhibit B, is the entire agreement of the parties concerning the Option and may be amended only in a writing signed by both parties. This Option Agreement may be executed in counterparts.

WITNESS the following signatures and seals:
